note: The Game's own sentences (noughts and crosses): B2 at its hardest. Never used by the Board, the Ultimate Challenge or Defuse.
focus: The passive at its hardest: reporting verbs, -ing and infinitive forms, and have something done.

rounds.prompt: The minister ___ to have resigned last night.
rounds.note: Subject + is reported + to have + past participle: the report is now, the resignation was last night.

rounds.prompt: I hate ___ what to do by people I've never met.
rounds.note: Hate + passive -ing: being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The bridge, which ___ at the moment, will reopen in May.
rounds.note: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The suspect is thought ___ the country last week.
rounds.note: Thought to have + past participle for an earlier action.

rounds.prompt: It ___ that the company will cut 500 jobs.
rounds.note: It is expected that …: an impersonal passive.

rounds.prompt: She can't stand ___ like a child.
rounds.note: Can't stand + being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The documents must ___ before the meeting started.
rounds.note: Must have been + past participle: a deduction about the past, in the passive.

rounds.prompt: Having ___ twice, the athlete was not allowed to compete.
rounds.note: Having been + past participle: a passive action that came first.

rounds.prompt: My phone ___ while I was on the train.
rounds.note: Get + past participle: an informal passive for something that happens to you.

rounds.active: They say the castle is haunted.
rounds.note: Subject + is said + to be.

rounds.active: Someone was following us when we left the club.
rounds.passive: We ___ when we left the club.
rounds.note: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle.

rounds.active: Someone should have told the passengers about the delay.
rounds.note: Modal perfect passive: should have been + past participle.

rounds.active: People believe that the thieves escaped through a window.
rounds.passive: The thieves are believed ___ through a window.
rounds.note: Believed to have + past participle: the escape came before the belief.

rounds.active: Nobody has watered these plants for weeks.
rounds.note: For weeks → present perfect passive.

rounds.prompt: The new stadium is expected ___ (complete) by next summer.
rounds.note: Expected + passive infinitive: to be + past participle.

rounds.prompt: I don't remember ___ (tell) about the change of plan.
rounds.note: Remember + being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The painting ___ (think) to have been stolen in the 1990s.
rounds.note: Is thought + to have been: thinking now about a past event.

rounds.prompt: By the time the firefighters arrived, most of the building ___ (destroy).
rounds.note: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: This form needs ___ (sign) by both parents.
rounds.note: Need + to be + past participle, or need + -ing with a passive meaning.

rounds.prompt: You'd better get that tooth ___ (check) before it gets worse.
rounds.note: Get something + past participle: someone else does it for you.

rounds.prompt: The match was called ___ because of the storm.
rounds.note: Call off = cancel; the particle stays with the verb in the passive.

rounds.prompt: She is said ___ have been the best student of her year.
rounds.note: Is said to have been.

rounds.prompt: He was made ___ apologise in front of the whole class.
rounds.note: Make someone do → be made to do: the to comes back in the passive.

rounds.prompt: Despite ___ given clear instructions, he got lost.
rounds.note: Despite + being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Is believed to have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle: someone did it for you.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Passive with a negative subject: not a word.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Past continuous passive.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: The window was broke last night.
rounds.answer: The window was broke last night.
rounds.note: The past participle is broken: was broken.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He is said to be very rich.
She is believed to have left.
It is thought that he lied.
They are said that they cheated.
rounds.answer: They are said that they cheated.
rounds.note: Either It is said that they cheated or They are said to have cheated.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He had cut his hair by his sister.
rounds.answer: He had cut his hair by his sister.
rounds.note: Causative order: He had his hair cut by his sister.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
rounds.note: Needs to fix has no object; the thing is fixed: needs to be fixed or needs fixing.

rounds.prompt: About now, or about the past?
items: He is said to live in Monaco.
She is believed to work for the BBC.
They are thought to be in hiding.
He is said to have lived in Monaco.
She is believed to have worked for the BBC.
They are thought to have escaped.
rounds.note: To + infinitive is about now; to have + past participle is about the past.

rounds.prompt: Correct or wrong?
items: It has been decided to wait.
The meeting was took place at noon.
The accident was happened at night.
rounds.note: Take place, happen and die have no object, so they have no passive.

rounds.prompt: Can the verb be passive?
rounds.note: Only verbs that take an object can be passive.

rounds.prompt: Match each sentence to its passive.
pairs: He is said to be a genius.
They said he was a genius.
He was said to be a genius.
They say he was a genius.
He is said to have been a genius.
They said he had been a genius.
He was said to have been a genius.
rounds.note: Is/was follows say/said; to have been shows the earlier time.

rounds.prompt: Match each active sentence to its passive.
rounds.note: The tense stays; be changes form.

rounds.prompt: People say that he is the richest man in Portugal.
rounds.stem: He ___ the richest man in Portugal.
rounds.note: Subject + is said + to be.

rounds.prompt: A mechanic is checking my brakes tomorrow.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle in the present continuous, for an arrangement.

rounds.prompt: They think the fire was started deliberately.
rounds.note: Is thought to have been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Nobody told me about the meeting.
rounds.note: The person told becomes the subject: I wasn't told.

rounds.prompt: They will have finished the work by Friday.
rounds.note: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: I don't like it when people tell me what to do.
rounds.stem: I don't like ___ what to do.
rounds.note: Like + being + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Someone needs to clean the windows.
rounds.note: Need + -ing has a passive meaning: they need to be cleaned.

rounds.prompt: They are building a new hospital near my house.
rounds.stem: A new hospital ___ near my house.
rounds.note: Present continuous passive.

rounds.sentence: My car needs to repair before the trip.
rounds.note: The car doesn't repair anything: needs to be repaired / needs repairing.

rounds.sentence: The accident was happened on a foggy night.
rounds.note: Happen has no object, so no passive.

rounds.sentence: He is believed to leave the country last week.
rounds.note: Last week is earlier than the belief: to have left.

rounds.sentence: The results will announce next Monday.
rounds.note: The results don't announce anything: will be announced.

rounds.sentence: She was made apologise to the whole class.
rounds.note: Made + to + infinitive in the passive.

rounds.sentence: It is said that he has been arrested last night.
rounds.note: Last night is a finished time: was arrested.
